title: Prefix key design + hit-velocity estimator for safe TTL annealing and rollbacks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce an automated recommendation and safe-apply workflow for KV/prefix caching that minimizes token cost while maintaining tail latency and model quality. This ticket scopes a new component: the Hit-Velocity Estimator (HVE), a collision-aware prefix hit predictor that drives probabilistic TTL annealing and staged rollback decisions.

Motivation: Existing autotuners assume stable prefix popularity and simple TTL heuristics. In practice we see bursty prefixes, prefix collisions across tenants, and cache pressure causing noisy hit-rate signals. The HVE will produce a short-term forecast (1–24h) of expected incremental hit-rate and cost-savings for candidate prefix key schemas and TTL ladders. It will also emit a safety score used by the rollout orchestrator to decide dark deploy / canary size / rollback thresholds.

Scope:
- Design metrics and data model for the HVE (hit velocity, collision delta, effective TTL utilization).
- Implement offline evaluator that replays request traces to measure estimator calibration.
- Add an API that proposes: (prefix-key-template, TTL-ladder, estimated_savings_pct, safety_score, recommended_canary_percent).
- Integrate with the existing rollout service to perform dark sampling + canary + automated rollback when safety score drops.

Non-goals: automatic model quantization or kernel-level runtime changes (these will be separate tickets). This ticket covers only keying/TTL recommendation and rollout orchestration for KV/prefix caching.
acceptance_criteria: HVE prototype computes a hit velocity and collision_delta metric for each prefix template with <=5% calibration error on replayed traces (1h and 24h horizons)
Recommendation API returns TTL ladder proposals and a numeric safety_score in [0,100] for any prefix template in production namespace
Rollout integration supports: dark sampling (0.5% of traffic) -> canary (configurable percent) -> automated rollback on safety_score deterioration
Console dashboard shows predicted savings, safety score, and recent rollout history per recommendation
implementation_plan: Design: define HVE signals and math (hit_velocity = d(H)/dt normalized by active_clients; collision_delta = expected false-shared-hits fraction)
Instrument: add lightweight prefix telemetry export in the runtime (summaries per 5m window: requests, unique_keys_est, avg_ttfu)
Offline evaluator: build a trace-replay harness that can test candidate key schemas and TTL ladders against historical traffic (support per-tenant and cross-tenant traces)
Estimator: implement HVE service (stateless inference over recent windows + simple exponential smoothing for velocity) and expose /v1/recommendations
Rollout: extend rollout service to accept HVE recommendations, run dark sampling and measure actual prefix hit delta; apply canary and monitor safety_score delta for automated rollback
Dashboard + Alerts: add runtime dashboard and alerting rules for safety_score < 40 or realized savings < 60% of predicted
metrics: tail_latency_p95 and p99 for cached requests
rollout_plan: 1) Nightly offline runs generate candidate recommendations and store in recommendations DB. 2) For each candidate: run dark sampling (0.5% traffic) for 30 minutes, measure observed_hit_delta and tail latency. 3) If safety_score >= 70 and observed metrics within thresholds, open canary at 2% for 2 hours. 4) Evaluate; if observed_savings >= 50% of predicted and tail latencies stable, promote to 25% then 100% over configurable windows. 5) If safety_score or observed metrics degrade by configured delta, trigger immediate rollback and a postmortem ticket. All steps are logged and reversible via the rollout UI.
risks: Estimator miscalibration for low-traffic prefixes (use Bayesian priors to reduce false confidence)
Cross-tenant collisions may cause overestimation of savings — need tenant-aware collision_delta accounting
Dark sampling might change cache dynamics; keep sample small and correct for sampling bias in estimator
Automated rollback on noisy signals could cause oscillations — implement hysteresis and min-stable-window guards
open_questions: What baseline prior should we use for very sparse prefixes? (Laplace smoothing vs hierarchical shrinkage)
Should safety_score include cost of rollback (operational overhead) or only user impact metrics?
How do we encode prefix templates that mix user-supplied IDs and normalized context (templating language)?
What signal source is authoritative for collision_delta: runtime sampled unique key count vs. application-provided cardinality hints?
notes: Design incorporates a conservative default: when in doubt, prefer shorter TTL and smaller canary. The HVE will be shipped in a read-only mode first (recommendations only) before enabling automated apply. Post-release: run a 4-week calibration window and iterate priors.
